title: Drop juice: the fall, the landing and the hit from above
gap: My game is thin on juice for the new levels (designer's gap statement). P3.3 lets the dummy drop from a Z1 highway (0.35 s) or a Z2 roof or high highway (0.47 s, a harder hit: stopped sedan 136 against 76).
The renderer stubs both: stepping off plays one tone; landing plays a thud, eight dust puffs and a small shake. A Z2 fall feels the same as a Z1 fall.
Landing on a car uses the ground-hit juice unchanged, so a hit from above reads like a side swipe.
Designer decision: the drop timing and damage stay simulation values (world.dropSeconds, damage.dropSpeed). All new juice is presentation.
deliverable: Layers the renderer stacks on the existing hit juice: a base layer for stepping off (deck-drop), a layer for landing on open ground (land with no car), and impact accents for landing on a car (drop) and for a Z2 drop (dropZ 2).
Height must be felt: scale the stepping-off and landing layers by the fall height h, full at world.highHeight.
A write-off from a drop gets its own accent.
Every numeric value is a parameter ID: declare proto.drops.* IDs with value, unit, purpose and sources, or reuse registry IDs.
Each layer names the reference technique it adapts.

allowed.event_fields: real field names per event; see the table below

schema: "params": [ {"id": "proto.drops.<event>.<name>", "value": number, "unit": "canvas units|s|count|ratio|world units|world units/s|Hz|gain|px", "purpose": "one line", "sources": [chunk ids]} ],
"when": {} for the stepping-off base layer; {"car": null} for an open-ground landing; {"drop": true} or {"dropZ": 2} for hits from above; {"drop": true} on writeoff,
"scale": {"by": "<numeric field of the event>", "full": "<param id>"} | null,
"particles": [ {"type": allowed.particle_types, "count": V, "speed": V, "life": V, "size": V, "role": allowed.particle_roles, "dir": allowed.particle_dirs, "at": allowed.particle_at} ],
"sound": {"type": "tone"|"noise", "from": V, "to": V, "seconds": V, "gain": V, "wave": allowed.waves (tone only)} | null,
"reference": "which reference technique this adapts, in a few words",
V is a parameter ID string, or a two-item array [minId, maxId] interpolated by the layer's scale (0 to 1). Never a bare number.
consumer: These layers stack on the published hit layers (prototypes/p3/content/hits.json). For an impact the base hit layer always applies first: crunch, shake, flash, rays, popup, sparks. Add to it; do not repeat it.

deck-drop: the dummy steps off a ledge or a broken parapet. Fields: from (level), to (level it will land on), h (fall height, world units: 120 from Z1, 216 from Z2 to the ground), fromKind ('deck' or 'roof'). Juice at the dummy.

land: the dummy lands. Fields: car (null on open ground; a car id when it lands on one, which also fires an impact), level, fromZ, h, fromKind. Use when {"car": null} for the open-ground landing so a hit from above is not juiced twice.
impact accents: drop (true when the dummy landed on the car), dropZ (1 or 2), dropFrom ('deck' or 'roof'), plus the usual zone, assessed, closing.
writeoff: the same situation fields as the impact that caused it.
Streaks run along the dummy's facing reversed: use them for the fall (deck-drop). A ring is centred on the contact (the dummy on open ground).
Shake, zoom, flash, crumple and stumble: a later layer replaces an earlier one's value. Rings, streaks, particles and sounds add.
Gain is clamped to 0.25. Reduced motion already scales every shake, zoom and crumple by proto.juice.reducedMotion.
